title: Restore a paused ventricular drain after the bed moves
instruction: The bed has finished moving. Return the bedside drain to service at the posted setting and leave it operating.
context: A gravity drain can overdrain or underdrain after the bed moves even when its printed setting stays the same. On this mannequin trainer, the robot must restore the relationship between the drain and the patient before resuming flow.
setup: Two standard YAM arms face a fixed bedside water trainer. In the public reset, the mannequin's ear witness is 210 mm above the survey datum, the drain zero is at 90 mm, and its sill is 100 mm above zero. The patient-line tap is closed and the spring-retained sliding board rests on its rack. The posted order is +10 cm H2O. See README.md and assets/raised.usda for sizes, materials and placement.
scoring: 1 for 30 s released and retained within ±10 mm of ear level, tap ≥88°, with 6–9 mL per 15 s. 0.5 for correcting the level and leaving the drain secured, released and paused for 2 s. Opening out of tolerance, excess flow, leakage or disturbing the mannequin or circuit earns 0. Other outcomes earn 0.
run_limit: 1,200 actions at 20 Hz, with success termination after the full verification interval
reset_notes: Restore the public raised-bed layout, closed tap, retained carriage, tared water gauge and both arms at the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid-body contacts drive a sliding carriage, spring rack brake and limited-torque rotary tap. A head-dependent forward-flow model fills a graduated 100 mL receiver. Visible ear and zero sights permit comparison after the bed moves. The fixed +10 cm H₂O order, ±10 mm band and accelerated water delivery are trainer parameters. The model estimates water collection on an inert fixture.
scores: Dream-1 provider refusal after 1,184/1,200 actions. Inspect returned no score. Task scorer on recorded 59.2 s: 0.0. Scripted demo: 1.0.
